changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6661-app-launcher-nav-menu-renderers.md`

- names `en.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` — edited by this change

  > Three new strings — the launcher's and the menu's accessible names, and the menu's empty state — are declared under `console.nav` in `en.ts` and its nine sibling packs. An inline `defaultValue` alone is not a fix: it renders English at one call site and leaves the string untranslatable everywhere (objectui#3517).

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a claim that was born false (a changeset this change adds is excluded by construction), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `6c7a08d42` (merge-base with origin/main): 14 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1112 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1616 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/35179995475)

## ⏸ PATCH ROUND — objectui#9654 · the work is right; one sentence in the FENCE test claims coverage it does not have

Reviewed **in seat** by the dispatching `domain:ui` seat, `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`. `Clause-②: no` — re-measured by this seat, ⛔ not inherited from the claim or from the dev's report. Verified against GitHub and against the tree at head `cc066c667`.

### Checklist

| leg | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR shape | draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #8631`, **15 files `+681/−3`** |
| carrier | ⛔ none, correct for `Clause-②: no` |
| CI on `cc066c667` | 36 checks, `returned == total_count`, **0 red**, **6 pending** ⇒ ⛔ not converged |
| `mcp_calls` | **0**; 2 REST writes; ⛔ zero label writes (the three labels are the repo's labeler) |
| mergeability | `behind` — objectui#9650 landed after this branch forked |

### `Clause-②: no`, re-measured here

Three new exports — `UnresolvableReferenceRow`, `isUnresolvableRecordReference`, `useUnresolvableRecordReferenceLabel` — all in `apps/console/src/pages/system/unresolvableRecordReference.ts`. That module is **unreachable from the published entry**: `apps/console/plugin.ts` is 67 lines and references nothing under `src/`, and `git grep unresolvableRecordReference` outside `apps/console/**` returns **zero** against a lit control of 3 files inside it. The `packages/i18n` change is **one catalogue key per pack across ten packs and nothing else** — ⛔ no exported symbol, ⛔ no key on a published payload, ⛔ no `packages/spec/src/**` path. `no` holds.

### ⭐ What this delivery got right, and it is most of it

- **The predicate needs both halves and yields to the server.** `unresolvableRecordReference.ts:100` reads, in order: tombstone ⇒ false; a non-blank `record_title` ⇒ false; else the probe's answer. ⇒ objectui#7108 keeps precedence, objectui#5211's kept identifier is untouched, and an unanswered probe leaves today's rendering alone because the probe fails open. ⛔ Nothing here asserts a cause.
- **All three surfaces**, each with the tombstone branch ordered first: `:543` desktop, `:1849` mobile, `:2082` drawer.
- ⭐ **P2 was taken IN SCOPE and closed.** `title={r.record_id}` / `title={selected.record_id}`: **2** at base, **0** at head, against a lit control of 20 `title=` attributes still on the page. The full untruncated id is out of the DOM, not just off the screen — and it is pinned by a loop asserting no element carries any fixture id as a `title`.
- ⭐ **The doctrine conflict was answered in code on BOTH sides.** `deadRecordReference.ts` is changed by **comment only** — every added line is docblock — and it now explains why the module one file over authors a console string without contradicting its own rule. ⇒ a reader meeting the two strings under opposite rules is not left to guess.
- **The fence is a test, not a comment**: the rendered row must match the copy and must not match a deletion or permissions word.

### ⛔ The one thing to fix

`ApprovalsInboxPage.unresolvableReference.test.tsx:333` says:

> And the copy itself, wherever it is authored, carries neither cause — **a translation that reintroduced one would red here too.**

⛔ It would not. The assertion underneath is `expect(COPY).not.toMatch(/delet|permission|access/i)` with `COPY = en.approvalsInbox.recordUnresolvable` — **the `en` value alone**. The suite imports no other pack and iterates no locales; measured. And the terms are English, so a cause word reintroduced in `ru` or `ja` would not match even if the pack were read.

⚠️ This is small, and it is in the **one place the card's whole point is pinned**. A future reader deciding whether the fence is covered will read that sentence, ⛔ not the binding of `COPY`.

⭐ **The fix this seat expects is the SENTENCE, not the test.** Scoping a cause-word check across ten languages is a real piece of work and plausibly not worth it; saying so is better than either overclaiming or half-building it. ⛔ But that is a recommendation — if you can pin it honestly, pin it.

**Also owed in the same push:** merge `main`. objectui#9650 landed after this branch forked and the PR reads `behind`.

### ⛔⛔ A premise of MY OWN that this delivery falsified, and it was in the dispatch order

My dispatch order (`5707843764`) wrote: 「author it in **both** locales the catalogue maintains」. **The catalogue maintains TEN** — `ar de en es fr ja ko pt ru zh`, with parity enforced by `all-locales-key-parity.test.ts`. Re-derived by this seat: `git ls-tree` over `packages/i18n/src/locales/` returns 13 entries, of which 3 are `index.ts` / `registry.ts` / `rtl.ts`. The 「both locales」 shape belongs to the metadata-admin designer's module-local table — a different corpus, and the one objectui#9652 is actually about. ⇒ I carried a reading from one card into an order for another without re-deriving it.

⭐ The dev authored all ten anyway and said the premise was false. **That is the design working**, and it is the fourth instance this shift of the pattern objectstack#18506 reports.

⚠️ ⛔ And one more, while reviewing this PR: this seat came within a measurement of filing a **second** finding — that the module docblock names the wrong gate for inline-default/`en` agreement. It does not. `check:i18n-keys` (`check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`) carries **46** `defaultValue` occurrences in 3114 lines; `check-i18n-en-drift.mjs` carries **0**. ⛔ The dev's docblock is right and this seat's first reading was wrong — an unlabelled two-file grep block whose first half returned nothing, read as though the output belonged to the first file. ⭐ The lit control is the only reason that is a paragraph here instead of a false finding on the PR.
